prompts.display_text: Pin a country with two or more temples announced or under construction.
prompts.text_original: A country with two or more temples announced or under construction (as of October 2026).
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, the Church has many temples announced or under construction around the world. The United States leads with 49, followed by Mexico with 13, Brazil with 12, the Philippines with 8, and Peru and Nigeria with 6 each. Countries such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Chile, Ghana and Mozambique also have more than one on the way.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Dale G. Renlund dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Dale G. Renlund dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Dale G. Renlund dedicated the Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple in 2019, the first temple in that country. He went on to dedicate Belém Brazil (2022), Cobán Guatemala and San Pedro Sula Honduras (2024), and Davao Philippines (2026).

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo (2019).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country other than the US where a member of the Quorum of the Twelve was born.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country other than the United States where a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles was born (through October 2026).
prompts.note: Uchtdorf's birthplace Ostrava is in today's Czechia, so only CZE is accepted, not SVK.
prompts.summary: Most members of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles were born in the United States, but many came from abroad. Six were born in England, from John Taylor to Patrick Kearon, and others came from Canada, Denmark, Norway, Ireland and Mexico. Dieter F. Uchtdorf was born in what is now Czechia, Ulisses Soares was the first from South America, and Gerald Causse of France was called in November 2025.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Six were born in England, from John Taylor to Patrick Kearon.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Ulisses Soares, the first from South America.

answers.name: Czechia
answers.fact: Dieter F. Uchtdorf, born in Ostrava, then Czechoslovakia.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Marion G. Romney, born in Colonia Juarez.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Marriner W. Merrill, born in New Brunswick.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: Charles A. Callis, born in Dublin.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country that Saints names as having stakes by the mid-2000s.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 35: by the mid-2000s these African countries had stakes. Pin one.
prompts.summary: By the mid-2000s the Church in Africa had grown enough to have stakes in many countries. Saints vol. 4 ch. 35 lists them, starting with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and including Kenya, the Republic of the Congo, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire, Liberia, Madagascar, Nigeria, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Named first in the chapter's list.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a land named in the Pentecost crowd (Acts 2:9-11) or Stephen's synagogue (Acts 6:9).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land named among Jews from abroad at Pentecost (Acts 2:9-11) or in the synagogue that disputed with Stephen (Acts 6:9)
prompts.summary: At Pentecost, Jews from many lands were in Jerusalem when the apostles were filled with the Holy Ghost, and each listener heard them speak in his own language (Acts 2:1-11). The crowd came from lands now in Israel, Iraq, Iran, Turkey, Egypt, Libya, Italy and Greece. About three thousand were baptized that day (Acts 2:41), and men from some of the same lands later disputed with Stephen (Acts 6:9).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia (Acts 2:9-10) and Cilicia (Acts 6:9) are all in Turkey.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Egypt is named among the homelands of the crowd, and Alexandrians disputed with Stephen (Acts 6:9).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Visitors from Rome heard the apostles at Pentecost (Acts 2:10).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Cretans were in the crowd; Crete belongs to Greece.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Mesopotamia, the land between the rivers, centres on Iraq.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Judaea is named among the lands of the crowd (Acts 2:9).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Parthians, Medes and Elamites came from lands in today's Iran.

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: The parts of Libya about Cyrene are in eastern Libya; Cyrenians also disputed with Stephen (Acts 6:9).
